title: U.S. House · Georgia's 10th District
area: East-central Georgia, including Athens, Madison, Milledgeville, and Covington.

context.text: This is an open seat: incumbent Mike Collins (R) withdrew from the Republican primary and is not on the November ballot for this district. Cook Political Report, Decision Desk, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball rate the general election Solid/Safe Republican.

candidates.name: Houston Gaines
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19 Republican primary over Ryan Millsap and Jeff Baker, 66.9%
candidates.currentRole: Member, Georgia House of Representatives, District 120 (since 2023)

summary.text: Houston Gaines is a Republican member of the Georgia House of Representatives from Athens, where he has served since January 2019. A University of Georgia graduate and former student body president, he has worked at Cannon Financial Institute and Carter Engineering and holds a House Republican leadership post. He won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary for the open 10th District seat.

background.text: Born January 11, 1995, in Athens, Georgia, according to Wikipedia; his campaign website says he was born and raised in Athens, is an eighth-generation northeast Georgian, and is the grandson of Superior Court Judge Joseph Gaines.
Graduated summa cum laude from the University of Georgia, where he was student body president; Wikipedia lists a B.A. in political science and economics in 2017.
Worked at Cannon Financial Institute, serving clients in the financial industry, and now works at Carter Engineering, which his legislative biography says he is helping expand.

Lost a 2017 special election for Georgia House District 117 to Democrat Deborah Gonzalez, then defeated her in a 2018 rematch and took office in January 2019; he was re-elected in 2020, 2022 and 2024. His district was renumbered 120 after redistricting.

According to his legislative biography, he was elected Majority Caucus Vice Chairman in 2022 and has served on committees including Ethics, Ways & Means, Appropriations, Insurance, Public Health and Governmental Affairs, as vice chairman of the Higher Education Appropriations subcommittee.

His legislative biography lists bills he authored on human trafficking, domestic violence, substance-abuse recovery, paid parental leave for teachers and state employees (2021), and prohibiting local governments from defunding police; his campaign website says more than 20 of his bills have passed.
Carried 2023 legislation creating a state oversight commission for district attorneys, which Gov. Brian Kemp signed in May 2023, according to Wikipedia.

Is a member of the Athens Rotary Club and has served on the Envision Athens Steering Committee, the Junior League of Athens Community Advisory Board and the LEAD Athens Alumni Association Board; his campaign website says he lives in Athens with his wife, Gabrielle.
Advanced from the May 19, 2026 Republican primary for the open 10th District seat, defeating Ryan Millsap and Jeff Baker; he is not seeking re-election to the state House.

priorities.text: Campaign says he "led the fight to crack down on illegal immigration at the state level and put a stop to sanctuary policies" and "helped craft legislation to rein in rogue district attorneys, like Fani Willis and Deborah Gonzalez."
Said in a campaign advertisement that the country needs "battle-tested, America-first warriors in D.C. to work alongside President Trump."

positions.summary: Campaign says he worked at the state level to crack down on illegal immigration and end sanctuary policies.

candidates.name: Pamela DeLancy
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19 Democratic primary over Lexy Doherty and John Dority, 54.4%

summary.text: Pamela DeLancy is the Democratic nominee in Georgia's 10th Congressional District. A retired U.S. Army nurse colonel, she spent her final six years in uniform at the Pentagon and is a licensed registered nurse. She won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary and is running on healthcare and veterans' issues.

background.text: Retired from the U.S. Army in 2019 as a nurse colonel; in her Candidate Connection survey she cites more than 30 years of service, and in interviews she has described nearly 40 years of military service.
Spent her last six years in the Pentagon, where The Red & Black reports she was director of medical readiness; she told Flagpole she wrote policies for veterans and service members.
Says she is a registered nurse with an active license and has treated patients in hospital settings.
Is a gallbladder cancer survivor who says she had two surgeries and six months of chemotherapy; her daughter lives with a rare disease.
Told Flagpole she is from Henry County and describes herself as "not a career politician."
Won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary, defeating Lexy Doherty and John Dority.

priorities.text: Says her focus "isn't on party politics" but on family issues, healthcare, and supporting veterans.
Cites her nursing and cancer-survivor experience in calling for "accessible, affordable healthcare that works for every family."

positions.summary: Campaign centers on "accessible, affordable healthcare," drawing on her nursing background and experience as a cancer survivor.
